cards.heading: Your brain on THC
cards.body: Cannabis triggers dopamine release in the brain's reward centre. Over time, your brain adapts by producing less dopamine naturally — which is why stopping can feel flat or anxious at first.

cards.statement: Most cravings last longer than 30 minutes if you don't use.
cards.explanation: Most cravings peak at around 20 minutes and fade on their own. Your job is simply to outlast the wave — not fight it.

cards.heading: Ride the wave
cards.body: Think of a craving as a wave. It builds, peaks, then crashes by itself. Surfers don't fight waves — they ride them. You can do the same.

cards.question: Why can quitting cannabis feel emotionally flat at first?

options.text: Your body forgets how to feel emotions
Your brain reduced its natural dopamine output

cards.explanation: Cannabis caused your brain to rely on external dopamine. It takes a few weeks to restore your natural baseline — it does come back.

cards.heading: It's not weakness
cards.body: Cravings are a normal brain response to habit disruption — not a character flaw. Having one doesn't mean you've failed. It means your brain is adapting.

cards.prompt: Think about the last time you had a craving. What were you doing? How long did it actually last before it faded on its own?
